title: A Teaspoon Weighs as Much as Mount Everest
dek: Neutron stars achieve densities of 10¹⁸ kg/m³ — the same density as atomic nuclei — packing 1.4 solar masses into a 10km sphere.
quote: 10¹⁸ kg/m³ — density of a neutron star
bullets: Degenerate neutron matter supported by neutron degeneracy pressure
Cross 2.17 M☉ and it collapses into a black hole

title: Little Green Men Was a Dead Star
dek: Jocelyn Bell Burnell's 1967 discovery of pulsars — initially labeled LGM-1 — revealed rotating neutron stars sweeping lighthouse beams across the galaxy.
quote: 1.33 seconds — the period of the first pulsar discovered
bullets: Jocelyn Bell Burnell, 1967: regular radio pulses
Pulsar = rotating neutron star, magnetic axis misaligned
Hulse-Taylor binary pulsar confirmed gravitational waves (Nobel 1993)
Fastest known: PSR J1748-2446ad spins at 716 Hz

title: The Line Between Star and Black Hole
dek: The TOV limit (~2.17 solar masses) is the maximum mass a neutron star can support. What's beyond that threshold — and what's inside — remains one of physics' open questions.
quote: TOV limit: ~2.17 M☉ — above this, collapse to black hole
bullets: Most massive measured: PSR J0740+6620 at 2.08 M☉
Inner core may contain hyperons, quark matter, or exotic states
NICER mission constrains radius via X-ray pulse profiles
GW170817 merger event confirms kilonova r-process nucleosynthesis
